name: Teri Clinic
tagline: Cosmetology and dermatology with a medical approach

listing.description: A website for a cosmetology, dermatology or aesthetic medicine clinic. A milky background with soft shader light, an italic serif, a price list of treatments as rows and doctors framed in arches.

seo.title: Teri Clinic — cosmetology and dermatology in Tashkent
seo.description: Dermatologist consultations, facial cleansing, peels, biorevitalisation and acne treatment. Doctors who specialise in dermatocosmetology, treatments only after an assessment, on Shakhrisabz Street.
seo.answer: Teri Clinic is a cosmetology and dermatology clinic at 16 Shakhrisabz Street in Tashkent, open Monday to Saturday from 10:00 to 20:00. A dermatologist consultation with a skin assessment is 200,000 UZS, a combined facial cleanse 350,000 UZS and a medium-depth peel from 450,000 UZS. Every treatment is prescribed only after a doctor’s consultation.

sections.title: Skin at ease
sections.subtitle: Our dermatologists look at the whole picture: cause first, treatment second. No unnecessary courses, no ‘filter-perfect’ promises.

sections.label: About
sections.title: A conversation first, then a treatment
sections.text: Teri Clinic was founded by dermatologists who were tired of seeing the after-effects of ‘just in case’ treatments. The first visit is a 40-minute assessment and a conversation about your skincare, lifestyle and expectations. If home care is enough, we’ll tell you. If a treatment makes sense, we’ll explain what it does, how many sessions it takes and what to expect in the first few days.

sections.label: Treatments
sections.title: Treatments and prices
sections.intro: Prices are per session. Your doctor decides on courses and combinations at the consultation.

items.title: Dermatologist consultation
items.text: A dermatoscope skin check, a review of your home care and a written plan.

items.title: Combined facial cleanse
items.text: Ultrasonic and manual extraction, finished with a calming mask.

items.title: Superficial peel
items.text: Mandelic or lactic acid to even out tone, with no downtime.

items.title: Medium-depth peel
items.text: For post-acne marks and pigmentation, in autumn and winter.

items.title: Biorevitalisation
items.text: Hyaluronic acid injections for hydration and skin density.

items.title: Acne treatment
items.text: A three-month plan: doctor visits, treatments where indicated and a check-in every four weeks.

items.title: Consultation
items.text: An assessment, questions about your care and health, and ‘before’ photos.

items.title: Plan
items.text: Home care and, if needed, treatments, with costs and timings.

items.title: Treatments
items.text: Done by the doctor who assessed you, with single-use materials.

items.title: Follow-up
items.text: A follow-up and photo comparison after 4–6 weeks.

items.quote: For the first time nobody tried to sell me a course at the door. The doctor cut my routine to three products and my skin finally calmed down.
items.author: Zarina A.

items.quote: I treated acne for three months. Everything followed the plan, with before-and-after photos and clear explanations at every step.
items.author: Madina T.

items.quote: A facial with no redness the next day. I went straight from the clinic to a meeting.
items.author: Oybek N.

items.q: Can I book a treatment straight away?
items.a: No: the first visit is always a consultation. It’s safer and saves you money on treatments you don’t need.
Yes: pregnancy, active inflammation and some medications and conditions. The doctor checks everything at the consultation.

items.q: When is the best time for peels?
items.a: Superficial peels can be done year-round with SPF; medium peels from October to March, when the sun is gentler.
Cash, Uzcard and Humo cards, Payme or Click. You pay after the treatment.

sections.label: Booking
sections.title: Book a consultation
sections.text: We reply on Telegram within an hour during opening hours and find you a doctor and a time.
